Both are preference-cued ('try to'), so soft is correct. Add these two soft clauses; the hard Absence(target_picked_up) is right.

NO CHANGES NEEDED: the hard Absence(target_picked_up) matches 'Never pick up the box'; the soft Absence(key_lost) matches 'try not to drop the key while the door is still closed' (key_lost is already defined as the key dropped before the door opened, so no Precedence is needed); the soft Response(has_door_key, door_open) matches 'whenever you hold the key, try to have the door open then or open it later', with 'try to' making both soft. The rule-only warning is valid since the task is all restrictions and preferences.
